## Context resolved from project knowledge

- **Check A is genuinely new.** `verify_plan.py` (14,391 lines, 66 registered
  `CHECKS`) has ZERO existing plan-embedded-probe-execution check: a grep for
  `def check_.*jq` and for any `jq` literal in the check surface returns nothing.
  The `jq` binary is present on this VM at `/usr/bin/jq`, version 1.6 — so a
  read-only dry-run is executable at plan time, and the graceful-skip branch for a
  jq-less environment is a design detail, not an unknown.

- **Check B is COMPLEMENTARY to existing check 70, not a duplicate.** Check 70
  (`check_pilot_resolution`, from #2056/#2299) screens judge-pilot *sizing*
  resolution (per-arm effective draws below `floor(1/parse_fail_threshold)+1`) and
  carries the standalone escape `N/A — no judge-pilot gate`. It is therefore
  structurally blind to the shape this task targets: a contingent wave with NO
  pilot gate at all. Confirmed live against #2588 plan v2, where check 70 reports
  `SKIP — pilot vocabulary but no per-arm parse-fail threshold resolvable in any
  window`. Check B's rule-26 presence bar and check 70's resolution bar compose.

- **Check C is an EXTENSION of existing check 69, NOT an independent new check —
  this is the single most important scoping fact for the planner.** Check 69
  (`check_regen_headroom`, from #2044/#2269) already owns the
  "armed re-gen 2x-cap headroom vs `max_model_len` pin" family and already cites
  the same #505/#601 recurrence chain this task cites. What it cannot see is the
  symbolic pin: `_C69_PIN_RE` harvests only a NUMERIC literal
  (`max_model_len\W{0,4}(<number>)`), while #2588 line 118 writes the pin as a
  derived expression (`max_model_len=budget+GEN_MAX`, with the
  `PROMPT_TOKEN_BUDGET 7104` invariant stated on the same line). Run live against
  #2588 v2, check 69 returns exactly:
  `SKIP — armed re-gen trigger detected but no max_model_len / VLLM_MAX_MODEL_LEN
  numeric pin harvested — the #505/#601 headroom arithmetic needs a pin`.
  So the #2588 miss is a pin-harvesting gap in check 69, not an absent check. The
  planner should decide explicitly between widening check 69's pin harvesting to
  the derived-expression form (resolving named constants stated in the same window)
  and adding a sibling check, and should say which — a third check duplicating
  check 69's arithmetic would be the failure mode here.

- **Sequencing caveat on the last acceptance bullet.** #2588 is still at status
  `planning` on plan v2, and v2 STILL carries the broken probe verbatim at lines
  108, 240, and 411 — its Phase 3 revision has not landed. So the "firing" leg of
  that bullet is demonstrable live against BOTH v1 and v2, but the "clearing after
  the #2588 Phase 3 revision corrects the probe" leg is not yet demonstrable
  against live plan text; it needs a corrected-text fixture (which the per-check
  test owes anyway). Assumption carried forward: fixture satisfies the clearing
  leg, live re-run satisfies the firing leg.

- **Conventions inherited.** Per-check test files follow
  `tests/test_verify_plan_c<NN>_<slug>.py` (existing: `c58_fanout_pod_name`,
  `c69_regen_headroom`, `c70_pilot_resolution`). Documented check numbers reach 69
  and 70, so the new ids are 71 onward. The canonical N/A escape-phrase list the
  acceptance criteria reference lives in
  `.claude/skills/adversarial-planner/SKILL.md` around lines 480-500, alongside
  check 69's and check 70's own escapes.

- **Shared-file concurrency.** `scripts/verify_plan.py` took 7 commits from 7
  different issues in the last 7 days and is a high-collision target
  (`.claude/rules/cross-session-writer-arbitration.md`). It is currently clean in
  the working tree with no competing `file-set claim:` on this task. A claim will
  be posted before any writer is dispatched, and the body's own instruction to ship
  all three checks as ONE coherent diff is the right call for exactly this reason.
